transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Well… I’m embarrassed to even say it out loud, but what finally made me come in is that after I eat too much, I’ve been going to the bathroom and making myself throw up. I tell myself it’s so I won’t gain weight, like I can undo what I just did, but it’s gotten past being some one-time awful mistake. It’s happened enough now that I scared myself, and I don’t feel like I can just pretend it’s nothing anymore.
Can you tell me more about these times when you make yourself throw up after eating—does it happen mostly when you feel especially worried about gaining weight, or is it more of a habit now?

It’s tied to the fear of gaining weight, yes… that’s the thought that’s in my head when I do it. It’s like after I’ve eaten too much, I panic and I think, “I have to get this out of me or it’s going to turn into weight.” And then I go to the bathroom and make myself throw up.

But I guess what scares me is that it doesn’t feel like just one terrible lapse in judgment anymore. At first I could tell myself, “Oh, that was a one-time thing, I was upset, I won’t do that again.” But now it’s become something I think of as an option after I overeat, like some part of me believes I can undo it. I hate saying that, because it sounds awful, but that’s really what finally made me come in. It’s not just a passing thought now—it’s something I’ve actually been doing.
How often have you been making yourself throw up after eating, and does it happen only after you feel you've overeaten, or have you done it even when you've eaten a normal or small amount?

It’s… it’s been most weeks now, for the last several months at least. I wish I could say it was just once in a while, like some rare bad day, but if I’m being honest, I can’t really call it occasional anymore.

It usually starts with one of those secret eating spells, where I feel like I’ve eaten too much and I’m ashamed, and then afterward I go and make myself sick. It’s not something I’m proud of at all. I’ve been trying to tell myself it isn’t that serious because it’s not every single day, but most weeks it happens, and that’s why I’m scared it’s become… I don’t know, more of a pattern than I wanted to admit.

Can you describe what happens before you go to the bathroom and make yourself throw up—do you find yourself eating a large amount of food in a short period of time, feeling out of control, or is it more that you eat a normal or small amount and still feel the urge to purge?

It’s definitely more after I’ve eaten a lot, not just a normal little meal. I mean… I suppose sometimes what feels like “too much” in my head might not look the same to someone else, but there are times when it really is a large amount.

Like if I’ve been out at bridge night, or I’ve worked a late shift and come home tired and wound up, I’ll start with something reasonable, like leftover casserole. And then I’ll go back and have more, and then maybe cookies I baked earlier, and then crackers, and then ice cream. It’s all in one sitting, sort of standing in the kitchen or going back and forth, not like sitting down with a plate like a normal person.

And it’s much more than I would ever put in front of anyone else. I’d be mortified if someone saw the amount. That’s usually when the panic comes in afterward, and then I go to the bathroom.
During these times when you eat a large amount of food, do you feel like you can't control yourself or stop eating even if you wanted to?

Yes… that’s probably the part that bothers me most, honestly. Once I get started during those times, it doesn’t feel like a normal choice anymore. It’s like I’m watching myself do it, almost on automatic.

I’ll be thinking, “Stop now, this is enough, don’t do this,” and at the same time I’m still reaching for one more thing. One more cookie, one more handful of crackers, whatever is there. And I’m also listening for my husband, worrying he’ll come in or notice what I’m doing, so there’s this frantic feeling of, “I should stop before he sees,” but I still keep going.

It’s embarrassing to admit, because I’m a grown woman and I know better. But in that moment it doesn’t feel like I’m calmly deciding to eat more. It feels like I’ve lost the brakes somehow.

The frequency and pattern described (occurring most weeks for several months) supports this diagnosis. No features suggestive of anorexia nervosa (F50.0) were endorsed.

inference_history.note: Initial presentation suggests potential eating disorder, specifically involving binge-eating and compensatory purging behaviors. Candidates include F50.2 (Anorexia nervosa purging type), F50.0 (Bulimia nervosa), and F98.2 (Eating disorder not otherwise specified, which may include atypical presentations). No differential ruled out yet.

The patient's behaviors and thoughts are primarily tied to a fear of gaining weight and recurrent episodes of self-induced vomiting after eating, which supports the retention of F50.2 (Bulimia nervosa) and F50.0 (Anorexia nervosa). F98.2 (Feeding disorder of childhood) was removed as the clinical picture is more consistent with an eating disorder typically seen in adolescents and adults rather than a childhood feeding disorder.

The patient's pattern of recurrent self-induced vomiting after eating, driven by fear of gaining weight, continues to support both anorexia nervosa (F50.0) and bulimia nervosa (F50.2). The behavior occurs multiple times per week over several months and is tied to body image concerns, without clear evidence yet to distinguish between restricting vs. binge-eating/purging subtypes. Further questioning is needed to determine the presence of binge-eating episodes and whether compensatory behaviors occur regularly in response to perceived overeating.
